meta.title: AlmostThere — turn any goal into today's checklist
meta.description: AI breaks your goal down into monthly milestones, weekly targets and a concrete daily checklist. Rest and reflection included, pace adapts to how you actually do.

hero.title: You're almost there.
hero.subtitle: Tell us your goal and your deadline. AI breaks it down into monthly milestones, weekly targets and a daily checklist you can actually tick off — with rest and reflection built into the plan.
hero.ctaNote: The demo needs no account. See how your goal breaks down in under a minute.
hero.trustLine: For freelancers, founders, networkers, students — and anyone who wants a life with something to show for it.

how.title: One goal. Three levels. Today's list.
how.subtitle: The whole product lives or dies on the quality of this breakdown, so that's where we put the work.

steps.title: You set the goal and the date
steps.body: "Reach A2 in German by the end of the year." That's enough. Add your rest and reflection preferences and we take it from there.

steps.title: AI builds the skeleton
steps.body: Monthly milestones first — what has to be done by the end of each month for the deadline to hold. Then each month splits into weekly targets.

steps.title: You get today's checklist
steps.body: Concrete tasks for today, sized to the time you actually have. Rest days and reflection blocks are items on the list, not gaps between them.

features.title: What makes it different
features.subtitle: Not another task list. A planner that actually gets you there.

items.title: Top-down breakdown that holds up
items.body: Goal → months → weeks → days. Every level is derived from the one above it, so the daily task you tick off today provably moves the deadline closer.

items.title: Several goals, one honest day
items.body: Your day is a fixed budget shared by every goal you're chasing. AlmostThere schedules across all of them at once, so two goals never quietly demand the same evening.

items.title: Rest is part of the plan
items.body: Say you want one task-free day a week, or ten minutes of reflection daily — and the AI plans around it. Rest shows up as a checklist item, because a plan that ignores recovery is a plan you'll drop.

items.title: The pace adapts to you
items.body: We track how much you actually complete. Falling behind for a couple of weeks? You'll get the choice: slow the plan down and move the date, or catch up and carry on unchanged. Nothing is ever rescheduled behind your back.

items.title: Milestones you look forward to
items.body: Attach your own reward to each milestone — or let the AI suggest a few, sized to what you just pulled off. Something small for a weekly milestone; for the finish line, something you'll remember.

example.title: What a breakdown looks like
example.subtitle: Goal: reach A2 in German. Deadline: six months. One rest day a week, ten minutes of reflection daily.
months: Core vocabulary (greetings, numbers, days), pronunciation of the alphabet, the 100 most common words
Present tense of regular and irregular verbs, simple sentences about yourself
Everyday vocabulary (shops, restaurants, travel), asking questions
Past tense (Perfekt), longer conversations, listening to simple texts
Vocabulary expanded to A2 level, reading simple texts
Practice and prep for the exam or real conversation, full A2 recap
weeks: Alphabet, pronunciation, greetings and basic phrases
Numbers 1–100, days of the week, months
First 50 most common words + simple phrases
Another 50 words, recap the month, self-test

days.text: Go through the alphabet and its pronunciation (20 min)
10 minutes — write down what was hardest to remember today

pricing.limitsTitle: What ten plans a month means
pricing.limitsBody: A new plan counts when you create a goal. Everything after that — the breakdown into weeks and days, the daily tasks, replanning when your pace changes — does not count and is unlimited for a running goal. Ten new plans is room to try different wordings and deadlines; someone who sets a goal and works on it will not use half of it in a month. The app shows you how much is left.

goals.title: Goals
goals.emptyBody: Set your first goal and the AI will break it down all the way to what you do today.

form.title: New goal
form.subtitle: Write down what you want to reach and by when. Treat the breakdown as a proposal you can change.

progress.note: The breakdown runs in the background. Do not close the page.

form.importanceLabel: How much does this goal matter to you
form.importanceHint: This decides how your daily time is split when several goals are running.

importance.5: This is the priority right now

form.colorHint: It tells you at a glance which task in your day belongs to which goal.
form.nameHint: Keep it to a few words. You will see it in your goal list and on daily tasks.
form.detailPlaceholder: What exactly you want to reach, what you already know, what limits you, how much time you will really give it, what matters most…
form.detailHint: This is the most important field on the page. It is what turns a generic plan into one that fits you — the more concrete you are, the better the result.
form.planningTitle: How this goal will be planned
form.planningHint: These three values decide what the AI plans for each of your days. They apply across all your goals.
form.planningKeepsDraft: What you have written is kept — you will come back here and lose nothing.
form.startPlaceholder: What you already know, have or have done in this area. „Completely from scratch“ is a fine answer too.
form.startHint: Without this the plan assumes you are starting from zero — and someone already part of the way there gets pointless first steps.

detail.expandHint: Detail is filled in as you go — always just for the nearest period. Further parts stay as a rough breakdown until you reach them.
detail.noDetail: Not broken down in detail yet
detail.deleteConfirm: This removes the goal together with its whole breakdown into periods, weeks and days. It cannot be undone.

overdue.title: {count, plural, one {One thing is left from earlier days} other {# things are left from earlier days}}
overdue.body: You can finish them, or let them go and move on. Either is fine — the plan will take it into account.
overdue.failed: That did not save. Please try again.

pace.title: {days, plural, one {One day did not get finished} other {# of the last days did not get finished}}
pace.body: Of everything that was already due, {percent}% got done. That is not a reproach, but the plan has to react — otherwise the remaining work gets squeezed into the time that is left and the deadline starts lying.
pace.catchUpBody: The deadline stays {date}. The rest of the plan gets rewritten so it can still be met — and I will tell you plainly whether it adds up.
pace.moveDeadlineBody: A new date based on the pace you are actually keeping: {date}. The plan gets rewritten at a calmer spread.
pace.later: Not now, ask me in a week

settings.title: How to plan
settings.subtitle: Every plan is built from these. The closer they are to reality, the less you will fight your own plan.
settings.capacityLabel: How much time you have for your goals each day
settings.capacityHint: In total, not per goal. Use the time you actually have, not the time you wish you had — a plan built on an inflated number cannot be kept, and stops being opened.
settings.restHint: Days off are part of the plan, not what is left over. No work gets scheduled on a rest day.
settings.reflectionHint: A short pause over what worked and what did not. Scheduled as its own task, not as an extra.
settings.timezoneHint: It decides when your new day starts. With the wrong zone you would see tomorrow's tasks in the evening.
settings.appliesNote: Changes apply from the next breakdown — each further week of your running goals gets laid out with the new values. Days already written stay as they are.

status.readyBody: This goal looks finished. Once you close it, I will add up what you went through and leave it here for you.
status.failed: That did not work. Please try again.
status.paused: This goal is paused. It gets no daily tasks and does not count towards your five running goals — the plan waits until you come back.
status.leftover: {count, plural, one {One task is still unfinished} other {# tasks are still unfinished}}. The plan is a proposal, not a condition — if the goal is reached as far as you are concerned, close it.

done.footnote: Welcome to the small fraction of people who not only set a goal but see it all the way through. Believe it or not, that is rare.
done.collectionEmpty: Once you finish a goal, it stays here.

milestones.title: Milestones and rewards
milestones.body: Every stage of the plan is a point where there is something to show. A long goal gives no feedback for months — the reward for a stage is what keeps it alive.
milestones.rewardPlaceholder: e.g. a whole afternoon with a book
milestones.failed: That did not work. Please try again.
milestones.reachedBody: By the plan, this stage should be behind you. Is it?

claim.body: {count, plural, one {A breakdown into one period} other {A breakdown into # periods}} is already done. You can take it over as it is — nothing gets generated again and it does not count towards your monthly limit.
claim.assumptionNote: The demo did not know how much time you have each day, so the plan was built on a general estimate. You now have {minutes} minutes a day set — once you start, the app will offer to recalculate if the pace does not fit.
claim.importanceLabel: How much it matters to you

importance.5: This is the priority right now

claim.detailPlaceholder: What you already know, what limits you, what matters most…
claim.detailHint: Saved with the goal. It will not change the breakdown you already have — it comes into play for later weeks and any replanning.

install.title: Add AlmostThere to your home screen
install.body: One tap opens it like any other app, with today’s tasks right there. Nothing to download from a store.

reminder.title: Daily reminder
reminder.body: Your phone will nudge you at the time you pick, even when the app is closed. The reminder is scheduled on the phone itself — nothing about it leaves for our server, and it works without a signal.
reminder.denied: Your phone has not allowed notifications for AlmostThere. You can turn them on in the phone's settings for this app.
reminder.notifyBody: Take a look at what you have planned.
